Round 2 of batch E's end-to-end screen (round 1 found seven defects, all repaired: `route-discover` ends a run whose discovery framed nothing — `initiative` has initial "" — before any sub-process fires; `read-order`/`route-order` gate authoring on the order's `checked` status; `route-checked` sends only `returned` back through the loop and ends the run on anything else, with a prose note on `pending-definition`; `more-features` reads the repository and the processed feature's status, both declared; feature-authoring's draft step now writes the feature's id into the initiative's Features section, and the initiative typedef names it as the §6 writer; O2's and O4's witnesses corrected).

The set:
NEW: basis/processes/product-flow.md (v2, 15 steps) + generated basis/skills/product-flow/SKILL.md (existence and step match only)
AMENDED: basis/processes/feature-authoring.md (v4: draft writes §6), basis/artifacts/initiative.md (v9: §6 writer named), .claude/shop/primer.md

Part 1 — product-flow against the process-definition chain (basis/artifacts/process-definition.md, basis/guidelines/process-definition.md, basis/fitness/process-definition.fitness.md): frontmatter, sub-process and run-step forms, labeled exits, prompts referencing only declared inputs, derived-check citations, CEL well-formed, branch reachability (no dead rows).

Part 2 — end-to-end trace: follow one initiative through the six sub-processes as product-flow invokes them; verify positional input lists against each child's parameter order; every routed status is one a child writes at that value; the else paths cover exactly what the children can leave; the §6 write by feature-authoring's draft supports more-features' judgment; no hand-off loses a value a later step needs.

Part 3 — the primer's claims against the corpus (the Current state's approval claims are true once this batch's block approval lands — treat product-flow's draft status as intended pre-approval state, not a finding; the product statement is owner-confirmed, not a finding).

Known and intended (not findings): the `completed` writer pending on the reconcile side; the register a feature to be built; the feature cap 24; O6-style empty outputs in the children; the post-cap/post-approval repairs disclosed in histories (this screen is their coverage — verify they cohere, report if they don't).

Do NOT run `git checkout`, `git restore`, or any command that modifies or reverts files. Read-only inspection; compiler dry-runs only into the scratchpad directory.

Return raw data, not a message: verdict "clean" or "findings", and for each finding: file, a short quote, and the defect in one sentence. Max 7 findings, worst first.

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

Each stage is its own defined sub-process with its own check; this process adds no judgment of its own — witnessed by every step being a sub-process, a runtime status read, route, or counter, or the PO role's continue decision. - O3. The feature loop exits when the PO role judges the initiative's features done, or at the feature cap — witnessed by `route-more`'s labeled branches. - O4. A run without an initiative — a cancelled discovery or a close without convergence — or without a bet ends with the records standing — witnessed by the else exits of `route-discover` and `route-bet`. **Roles:** the sub-processes' own roles, unchanged by this process; plus the [PO role](../roles/lead-po.md) at `more-features` (judges, from the initiative's Features section and the backlog order, whether the initiative needs another feature — an exercise of its backlog accountability, not a check). **Carried by:** [`../skills/product-flow/SKILL.md`](../skills/product-flow/SKILL.md) — generated from this definition by [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never edited by hand. ## Flow (compiled) Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not edit by hand. ```mermaid flowchart TD discover{{"Discover the problem — sub-process: discovery-conversation-process
in — topic: string, form: string
out — initiative: string"}} route_discover{"Route on the discovery
in — initiative: string"} check{{"Check the initiative and take the bet — sub-process: initiative-check-process
in — initiative: string, initiative_criteria: string, contracts: string, repository: string, experience_principles: string, core_tasks: string
out — initiative: string"}} read_bet["Read the initiative's status — runtime
in — initiative: string
out — initiative_status: string"] route_bet{"Route on the bet
in — initiative_status: string"} place{{"Place the initiative in the backlog order — sub-process: backlog-ordering-process
in — initiative: string, order: string, priority: string, recommendations: string, order_criteria: string
out — new_order: string"}} read_order["Read the order's status — runtime
in — new_order: string
out — order_status: string"] route_order{"Route on the order's check
in — order_status: string"} author{{"Author and check one feature — sub-process: feature-authoring-process
in — initiative: string, repository: string, decomposition: string, experience_principles: string, core_tasks: string, feature_criteria: string
out — feature: string"}} read_feature["Read the feature's status — runtime
in — feature: string
out — feature_status: string"] route_checked{"Route on the check
in — feature_status: string"} assign{{"Assign the feature's scenarios — sub-process: scenario-assignment-process
in — feature: string, decomposition: string, contracts: string, repository: string
out — feature: string"}} more_features(["Judge whether the initiative needs another feature — agent: lead-po
in — initiative: string, new_order: string, repository: string, feature_status: string
out — more: string"]) advance_feature["Advance the feature count — runtime
in — feature_count: integer
sets — feature_count: integer"] route_more{"Route on the PO role's judgment
in — more: string, feature_count: integer, feature_cap: integer"} __end(("end
result — initiative: string")) __start(("start")) --> discover discover --> route_discover route_discover -->|framed — an initiative stands proposed| check route_discover -->|else| __end check --> read_bet read_bet --> route_bet route_bet -->|bet — the initiative is planned| place route_bet -->|else| __end place --> read_order read_order --> route_order route_order -->|checked — proceed to authoring| author route_order -->|else| __end author --> read_feature read_feature --> route_checked route_checked -->|checked — assign its scenarios| assign route_checked -->|returned — back through the PO role's judgment for another pass| more_features route_checked -->|else| __end assign --> more_features more_features --> advance_feature advance_feature --> route_more route_more -->|success exit: the initiative's features are done and assigned| __end route_more -->|failsafe exit: feature_count >= feature_cap — the run ends with the initiative's state recorded| __end route_more -->|else| author ``` ## Data Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema names inline; every structured shape is a `$ref` to a defined type with an explicit source. Conditions are CEL expressions over these names. A sub-process step's inputs map positionally to its child's parameters, so each criteria set is declared under its own name here — `initiative_criteria`, `feature_criteria`, `order_criteria` — and mapped to the child's `criteria_path`. `contracts`, `repository`, `decomposition`, `experience_principles`, `core_tasks`, `order`, `recommendations`, and `priority` are the lead-shop-held records the sub-processes declare; their meanings are those documents'. The status reads are `run` steps: a stage's outcome is the status its own record step wrote, and this process routes on that status, never on a judgment of its own. ```yaml data: topic: {type: string} form: {type: string, enum: [brainstorm, interview, review-of-evidence]} initiative_criteria: {type: string, format: uri-reference} feature_criteria: {type: string, format: uri-reference} order_criteria: {type: string, format: uri-reference} contracts: {type: string, format: uri-reference} repository: {type: string, format: uri-reference} decomposition: {type: string, format: uri-reference} experience_principles: {type: string, format: uri-reference} core_tasks: {type: string, format: uri-reference} order: {type: string, format: uri-reference} priority: {type: string, format: uri-reference} recommendations: {type: string, format: uri-reference} initiative: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: ""} new_order: {type: string, format: uri-reference} feature: {type: string, format: uri-reference} initiative_status: {type: string} order_status: {type: string} feature_status: {type: string} more: {type: string, enum: [another, done]} feature_count: {type: integer, initial: 1} feature_cap: {type: integer, initial: 24} ``` ## Steps ```yaml start: discover parameters: [topic, form, initiative_criteria, feature_criteria, order_criteria, contracts, repository, decomposition, experience_principles, core_tasks, order, priority, recommendations] result: initiative steps: - id: discover name: Discover the problem run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: discovery-conversation-process, from: discovery-conversation.md} inputs: [topic, form] outputs: [initiative] next: route-discover - id: route-discover name: Route on the discovery run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [initiative] branches: - label: "framed — an initiative stands proposed" when: initiative != "" next: check - else: end - id: check name: Check the initiative and take the bet run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: initiative-check-process, from: initiative-check.md} inputs: [initiative, initiative_criteria, contracts, repository, experience_principles, core_tasks] outputs: [initiative] next: read-bet - id: read-bet name: Read the initiative's status run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [initiative] outputs: [initiative_status] run: | sed -n 's/^status: //p' ${initiative} next: route-bet - id: route-bet name: Route on the bet run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [initiative_status] branches: - label: "bet — the initiative is planned" when: initiative_status == "planned" next: place - else: end - id: place name: Place the initiative in the backlog order run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: backlog-ordering-process, from: backlog-ordering.md} inputs: [initiative, order, priority, recommendations, order_criteria] outputs: [new_order] next: read-order - id: read-order name: Read the order's status run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [new_order] outputs: [order_status] run: | sed -n 's/^status: //p' ${new_order} next: route-order - id: route-order name: Route on the order's check run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [order_status] branches: - label: "checked — proceed to authoring" when: order_status == "checked" next: author - else: end - id: author name: Author and check one feature run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: feature-authoring-process, from: feature-authoring.md} inputs: [initiative, repository, decomposition, experience_principles, core_tasks, feature_criteria] outputs: [feature] next: read-feature - id: read-feature name: Read the feature's status run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [feature] outputs: [feature_status] run: | sed -n 's/^status: //p' ${feature} next: route-checked - id: route-checked name: Route on the check run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [feature_status] branches: - label: "checked — assign its scenarios" when: feature_status == "checked" next: assign - label: "returned — back through the PO role's judgment for another pass" when: feature_status == "returned" next: more-features - else: end - id: assign name: Assign the feature's scenarios run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: scenario-assignment-process, from: scenario-assignment.md} inputs: [feature, decomposition, contracts, repository] outputs: [feature] next: more-features - id: more-features name: Judge whether the initiative needs another feature run-by: {role: lead-po, execution: agent} inputs: [initiative, new_order, repository, feature_status] outputs: [more] prompt: | Read the initiative's Features section — the features this and earlier passes made, by id — the backlog order at new_order, the status feature_status of the feature just processed, and, for the listed features, their statuses in the feature repository at repository. Judge whether the initiative needs another feature — a behavior its framing serves that no feature yet states, or a returned feature to author again — or whether its features are done and every one is assigned. Return "another" or "done". This is your backlog accountability, not a check: the framing decides what is needed, the appetite bounds it. next: advance-feature - id: advance-feature name: Advance the feature count run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [feature_count] set: feature_count: feature_count + 1 next: route-more - id: route-more name: Route on the PO role's judgment run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [more, feature_count, feature_cap] branches: - label: "success exit: the initiative's features are done and assigned" when: more == "done" next: end - label: "failsafe exit: feature_count >= feature_cap — the run ends with the initiative's state recorded" when: feature_count >= feature_cap next: end - else: author ``` A discovery that cancels or closes without convergence leaves no initiative — `route-discover` ends the run with the conversation's record standing. A `returned` feature goes back through the PO role's judgment for another authoring pass; a `pending-definition` feature, and an order that is not `checked`, end the run — the definition change or re-placing they await is decided outside this flow, and a new run resumes when it lands. ## Derived checks | Outcome | Check | Kind | Where | |---|---|---|---| | O1 | `assign` reachable only through `route-bet` ("planned"), `route-order` ("checked"), and `route-checked` ("checked") | mechanical | branch graph | | O2 | every step is a sub-process, a runtime status read, route, or counter, or the `more-features` judgment | mechanical | step list | | O3 | `route-more` carries the success and failsafe exits, labeled | mechanical | `route-more.branches` | | O4 | the no-initiative and no-bet else exits end the run with the records standing | mechanical | `route-discover.branches`, `route-bet.branches` | ## Document History | Version | Date | Kind | Entry | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 2026-08-31 | update | Authored as batch E of brief-032's plan: the top-level flow the model names — discovery to assignment, each stage its own sub-process, routing only on statuses the stages wrote, the feature loop exited by the PO role's done judgment or the feature cap. | | 2 | 2026-08-31 | update | Batch C screen round 1 (carried into this draft): the enabler recommendations parameter passed through to backlog-ordering. | | 3 | 2026-08-31 | review | Batch E end-to-end screen round 1: route-discover ends a run whose discovery framed nothing before any sub-process fires; the order's check status gates authoring (read-order/route-order); pending-definition ends the run instead of looping under unchanged criteria; more-features reads the repository and the processed feature's status, both declared; O2's and O4's witnesses corrected. |

===== artifacts/process-definition.md =====
     1	---
     2	type: artifact-typedef
     3	id: process-definition-typedef
     4	defines: process-definition
     5	owner: product-authority
     6	status: approved
     7	approved: 2026-08-22
     8	version: 6
     9	created: 2026-08-19
    10	updated: 2026-08-28
    11	ancestry: [definition, process-definition]
    12	---
    13	
    14	# Artifact type: process-definition
    15	
    16	## Identity and ancestry
    17	
    18	- **Type:** `process-definition` — the single source of truth for a
    19	  process: what it is for, what a run produces, and every step in a form
    20	  a runtime can construct a workflow from. Skills, flow
    21	  diagrams, and fabro graphs (fabro is the fleet's workflow-orchestrator
    22	  runtime) are its renderings.
    23	- **Produced by:** seed drafting or governed evolution. **Consumed by:**
    24	  the compiler (renderings), agents (via the rendered skill), reviewers
    25	  (conformance and loop-exit review), fabro (via annotations).
    26	
    27	## Required frontmatter
    28	
    29	`type: process-definition`, `id`, `owner`, `status`, `created`,
    30	`updated`; `produces` (artifact
    31	types a run creates; the generic root `definition` covers runs creating
    32	definition documents; empty when the run's value is state change);
    33	`condition-language: cel`; optional: `carried-by` (the rendered skill's
    34	id), `condition-functions` (declared extensions, name and signature),
    35	`annotations` (process-level rendering metadata, keyed by rendering
    36	target); `hold-after` (ISO 8601 duration — the inactivity window after
    37	which the runtime holds a run; required for any process that carries a
    38	conversation); `ask-cap` (ISO 8601 duration — how long an ask may stand
    39	unanswered before its default applies; required for any process whose
    40	steps carry `asks`).
    41	
    42	## Required sections
    43	
    44	1. **Purpose** — one short paragraph.
    45	2. **Guiding statement** (optional) — directs judgment across the whole
    46	   process; the compiler copies it into every rendering.
    47	3. **Outcomes** — each names the step or check that witnesses it.
    48	4. **Roles** — roles and their accountability; role files carry identity,
    49	   never sequencing.
    50	5. **Flow (compiled)** — the diagram generated from the steps; never
    51	   edited by hand.
    52	6. **Data** — process-local value names. Simple types (JSON Schema
    53	   primitives) inline; every structured shape is a `$ref` to a defined
    54	   type with an explicit source: `from:` is a relative link to the
    55	   defining file, or `pkg:<package>/<type>` when the type lives in
    56	   another package and is fetched through that package's contract tool
    57	   (e.g. `shop-knowledge schema session-record`). Every distinct `$ref`
    58	   carries `from:` at least once; the linter verifies local sources
    59	   define the referenced type. No structured shape is ever defined here.
    60	   A value may declare `initial` — its value at run start.
    61	7. **Steps** — the executable part (shape below).
    62	8. **Derived checks** — a table: outcome, check, kind, where; every row
    63	   cites its clause or is deleted.
    64	
    65	Header elements 1–4 are bolded labels before the first heading; 5–8 are
    66	markdown headings in order (a section is a heading, per the
    67	artifact-typedef rule).
    68	
    69	## The steps section
    70	
    71	Top-level keys: `start` (first step id); optional `parameters` (data
    72	values supplied at instantiation rather than produced by any step);
    73	optional `result` (the data value a run returns — the artifact, not a
    74	status record; omit only when the outcomes pin the run's value). `end`
    75	is the reserved terminator id for `next`. Each step:
    76	
    77	- `id`, `name`; `run-by` — `{role, execution: agent}`,
    78	  `{role, execution: human}` (a role a person holds, e.g. an authority review), or `{execution: runtime}`; `fresh-context: true` where a role
    79	  must not carry memory between runs.
    80	- `inputs` / `outputs` — lists of declared data names; the typed contract
    81	  is the isolation mechanism (a step reads only what it lists).
    82	- Agent and human steps carry `prompt` — **the only prose allowed in a
    83	  step** (for a human step it is the question the review puts).
    84	- Runtime steps carry `set` (CEL assignments to data values or their
    85	  fields), `run` (command templates
    86	  with `${...}` interpolation from typed inputs — a scalar interpolates
    87	  as its value, an array as one shell word per element, a field of an
    88	  array's items as `${name[].field}` yielding one word per item in
    89	  item order, so a template may run a shell `for` over it or pair two
    90	  such fields positionally; `name` may be a data name or a field path
    91	  into one. A `run` step yields at most one output: the template's
    92	  standard output — split by line for an array value; `atomic: true`
    93	  binds the lines into one all-or-nothing act), or `branches`.
    94	- `checks` — CEL expressions over declared data.
    95	- Routing: `next`, or `branches` of `{label, when (CEL), next}` rows plus
    96	  one `else`. **Every loop declares its exits as labeled branch rows** —
    97	  a reached-state success exit, a round or budget cap, or both.
    98	- `asks` — optional list of role ids the step may put an ask to (the
    99	  [`ask`](../types/ask.md) data type). An agent or human step listed
   100	  with `asks` may return an ask in place of its outputs; a step without
   101	  `asks` may not ask. A process with asking steps declares an `ask` data
   102	  value (`$ref: ask`) and lists it in each asking step's inputs. Every
   103	  ask names a `default` and a `checkpoint`; the step's prompt states
   104	  what kind of information it may ask for — never a judgment the step's
   105	  role owes. A step returns at most one ask per run — the loop's exit —
   106	  and a second resolves `defaulted` at once. Early steps ask cheaply;
   107	  an ask from a late step wastes the work not in its checkpoint.
   108	- `annotations` — per-step rendering metadata keyed by target (e.g.
   109	  `fabro: {model, max_attempts}`); the definition itself ignores them.
   110	- `run-by: {execution: sub-process, process: <process-id>, from: <source>}`
   111	  runs another process definition as one step: the step's inputs map to
   112	  the child's parameters and its outputs receive the child's result. A
   113	  conversation invoked this way is a branched conversation: the child's
   114	  anchor records the parent run.
   115	
   116	## Run lifecycle
   117	
   118	A run is one execution of a process, anchored to a work item in the
   119	registry. Run states: `running`, `held`, `done`, `cancelled`.
   120	
   121	- **Hold** pauses a run: the current step and every data value persist in
   122	  the run's anchor, and the work item records the state. A held run is
   123	  resumed at its recorded step or cancelled with a reason — never
   124	  silently dropped.
   125	- The `hold-after` window makes parking automatic: a run with no activity
   126	  inside the window is held by the runtime. Unfinished work parks itself
   127	  with a named resume point; nothing dangles in the lead repo.
   128	- **Ask** holds a run the same way, with the ask recorded on the anchor
   129	  and routed to whoever fills the role it names — a person or an agent;
   130	  the answer is written to the ask and the run resumes at the asking
   131	  step with the ask in its inputs, in a fresh context loaded from the
   132	  step's declared inputs and the checkpoint. There is no synchronous
   133	  form: no step waits in place for an answer. An unanswered ask resolves
   134	  to its `default` at the process's `ask-cap` (an ISO 8601 duration,
   135	  required for any process whose steps carry `asks`), and the run
   136	  resumes on the default with the ask marked `defaulted`; cancelling a
   137	  held run marks its ask `cancelled`. Answering is an activity of the
   138	  answering role: a human step for a human-held role, or a step the
   139	  answering role's process names — those steps are defined in the
   140	  processes that answer, not here. The registry that anchors runs
   141	  records every ask; asks per run, per role, and per kind are read from
   142	  it. An ask that recurs across runs is a gap in a definition; the
   143	  answering role files the definition change, and the ask stops.
   144	- **Cancel** closes the run's work item with a reason and files the
   145	  resulting actions the outcomes demand.
   146	
   147	## Rendering contract
   148	
   149	The compiler generates: the in-document flow diagram (typed inputs and
   150	outputs on every node; the result on the end node) and the skill —
   151	front-matter (`generated: true`, `generated-by`, `derived-from`,
   152	`source`, `source-digest`) and body (purpose, guiding statement, result,
   153	diagram, one section per step with the prompt verbatim). Conformance
   154	check: re-run the compiler and diff.
   155	
   156	## Commitment (Definition of Done)
   157	
   158	A process definition is done when it compiles — every `$ref` resolves,
   159	the diagram and renderings generate, `result` (if declared) names a data
   160	value — and every loop declares its exit. **Consequence on failure:** it
   161	cannot be dispatched, carried by a skill, or cited by a check.
   162	
   163	## Sources
   164	
   165	ISO/IEC/IEEE 24774 (name/purpose/outcomes header); GitHub Actions (step
   166	records with typed inputs/outputs); CNCF Serverless Workflow
   167	(data-condition transitions); CEL — Common Expression Language
   168	(mechanically translatable conditions); Essence-style state exits plus a
   169	round cap (the dual-exit rule).
   170	
   171	## Derived review checklist
   172	
   173	- Compiles clean: refs resolve, diagram and renderings regenerate
   174	  byte-stable. *(Commitment)*
   175	- No prose inside step records outside `prompt` fields; section
   176	  introduction prose is body text, not step content. *(§The steps section)*
   177	- Every loop has labeled success and/or cap exits. *(§The steps section)*
   178	- Every step with `asks` belongs to a process with `ask-cap` and lists
   179	  the `ask` value in its inputs; every ask names a default and a
   180	  checkpoint, and its `to` is in the step's `asks`; one ask per step per
   181	  run. *(§The steps section, §Run lifecycle)*
   182	- Outcomes each name a witness. *(§Required sections 3)*
   183	- `result`, if absent, is justified by outcomes that pin the run's value.
   184	  *(§The steps section)*
   185	
   186	## Document History
   187	
   188	| Version | Date | Kind | Entry |
   189	|---|---|---|---|
   190	| 1 | 2026-08-19 | update | Authored (seed layer); earlier history, if any, in the repository history. |
   191	| 1 | 2026-08-22 | state | draft → approved. |
   192	| 2 | 2026-08-23 | update | Owner direction: decision-ledger references removed — changes stand on their own; history entries and text no longer cite numbered decisions. |
   193	| 3 | 2026-08-25 | update | Owner direction: a near-synonym of "role" retired and banned. |
   194	| 4 | 2026-08-25 | update | Owner decision: the ask mechanism defined, held-and-resumed only — a step may carry `asks` (role ids) and return an `ask` data value in place of its outputs; the run holds, the role answers, the step resumes in a fresh context from its inputs and the ask's checkpoint; `ask-cap` bounds an unanswered ask with its default; a recurring ask is a definition gap. No synchronous form. |
   195	| 4 | 2026-08-25 | review | Screened with the ask data type: findings — the ask loop lacked an exit; the resumed ask had no data name; answering had no named activity; the recurrence measure had no channel; an old use of "ask" collided. Repaired in place: one ask per step per run, the `ask` value declared and listed, answering placed in the answering role's process, the registry named as the count's home, wording fixed. |
   196	| 5 | 2026-08-28 | update | Owner direction, from the scenario-assignment screen: how arrays and item fields interpolate into a `run` template defined, so a fan-out over contexts is a defined form. |
   197	| 6 | 2026-08-28 | update | From the scenario-assignment screen: how a `run` step yields its output (standard output, line-split for arrays) and that interpolation names may be field paths — both were silent conventions. |
===== guidelines/process-definition.md =====
     1	---
     2	type: quality-guideline
     3	id: process-definition-guideline
     4	target-type: process-definition
     5	owner: product-authority
     6	status: approved
     7	approved: 2026-08-23
     8	version: 1
     9	created: 2026-08-23
    10	updated: 2026-08-23
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Guideline: process definition
    14	
    15	**Voice principle.** Write for the runtime that must construct a
    16	workflow from the steps and the reviewer who must connect every
    17	outcome to its witness: every element either executes, routes,
    18	witnesses, or declares a contract — explanation lives in body prose,
    19	never inside a step.
    20	
    21	**Highlights (the layer compiled into generating context):** every
    22	outcome names its witness · prose inside a step only in `prompt` ·
    23	every loop declares a labeled success exit, a cap, or both · a step
    24	reads only what it lists — the declared list is the context load list ·
    25	the result is the artifact, not a status.
    26	
    27	**Layers:** this guideline adds process-definition rules on top of the
    28	[base writing style](base-writing-style.md); the base always applies
    29	and is never overridden. When rules conflict, an approved principle
    30	beats the
    31	[process-definition typedef](../artifacts/process-definition.md),
    32	which beats this guideline.
    33	
    34	---
    35	
    36	## Rules
    37	
    38	**1. Give every outcome a witness.**
    39	Before: "O1. The review is high-quality."
    40	After: "O1. Every decision is applied before the next exchange —
    41	witnessed by the check on `apply`."
    42	*Test:* read each outcome. *Criterion:* it names the step, check, or
    43	branch that witnesses it, and that witness exists in the steps
    44	section. *Decision:* yes/no per outcome.
    45	*Derived check:* judged — scenario 2 of
    46	[process-definition.fitness.md](../fitness/process-definition.fitness.md).
    47	
    48	**2. Keep prose out of steps.**
    49	Before: a step record carrying "This step is important because
    50	reviewers often forget to check the register."
    51	After: the sentence moved to body text before the steps section, or
    52	into the step's `prompt` if the agent needs it.
    53	*Test:* scan every step record. *Criterion:* prose appears only in
    54	`prompt` fields; runtime steps carry `set`, `run`, or `branches` and
    55	no sentences. *Decision:* yes/no per step.
    56	*Derived check:* mechanical — the no-prose row of the typedef's
    57	derived review checklist.
    58	
    59	**3. Declare every loop's exits, labeled.**
    60	Before: revise → review → revise with no cap and an unlabeled edge.

    67	the loop-exit row of the typedef checklist.
    68	
    69	**4. Let a step read only what it lists.**
    70	Before: a prompt telling the agent to "check the register and any
    71	related records you find useful."
    72	After: the register declared as an input; the prompt references only
    73	declared inputs.

    75	declared inputs and outputs. *Criterion:* every reference resolves to
    76	a declared name; the declared list is the step's context load list —
    77	an undeclared load is a defect. *Decision:* yes/no per step.
    78	*Derived check:* judged — fitness scenario 4.
    79	
    80	**5. Return the artifact, not a status.**
    81	Before: "result: report — a summary of what the run did."
    82	After: "result: set — the principle-set the run produced."

    84	the run returns the artifact it exists to produce, or omits `result`
    85	with outcomes that pin the run's value. *Decision:* yes/no per
    86	process.

    88	
    89	**6. Direct judgment with the guiding statement, not instructions.**
    90	Before: "Guiding statement: first draft, then review, then ship."
    91	After: "Guiding statement: everything binding lands in the governed
    92	artifacts it changes; nothing binding lives only in the transcript."

    94	that applies across every step, never a sequence — sequences are
    95	steps. *Decision:* yes/no per statement (vacuously pass when absent).
    96	*Derived check:* judged — fitness scenario 6.

    55	   defining file, or `pkg:<package>/<type>` when the type lives in
    56	   another package and is fetched through that package's contract tool

    58	   carries `from:` at least once; the linter verifies local sources
    59	   define the referenced type. No structured shape is ever defined here.

    69	## The steps section
    70

    72	values supplied at instantiation rather than produced by any step);

   112	  the child's parameters and its outputs receive the child's result. A
   113	  conversation invoked this way is a branched conversation: the child's
   114	  anchor records the parent run.

   116	## Run lifecycle
   117	
   118	A run is one execution of a process, anchored to a work item in the
   119	registry. Run states: `running`, `held`, `done`, `cancelled`.
   120	
   121	- **Hold** pauses a run: the current step and every data value persist in
   122	  the run's anchor, and the work item records the state. A held run is
   123	  resumed at its recorded step or cancelled with a reason — never
   124	  silently dropped.
   125	- The `hold-after` window makes parking automatic: a run with no activity
   126	  inside the window is held by the runtime. Unfinished work parks itself
   127	  with a named resume point; nothing dangles in the lead repo.
   128	- **Ask** holds a run the same way, with the ask recorded on the anchor
   129	  and routed to whoever fills the role it names — a person or an agent;
   130	  the answer is written to the ask and the run resumes at the asking
   131	  step with the ask in its inputs, in a fresh context loaded from the
   132	  step's declared inputs and the checkpoint. There is no synchronous
   133	  form: no step waits in place for an answer. An unanswered ask resolves
   134	  to its `default` at the process's `ask-cap` (an ISO 8601 duration,
   135	  required for any process whose steps carry `asks`), and the run
   136	  resumes on the default with the ask marked `defaulted`; cancelling a
   137	  held run marks its ask `cancelled`. Answering is an activity of the
   138	  answering role: a human step for a human-held role, or a step the
   139	  answering role's process names — those steps are defined in the
   140	  processes that answer, not here. The registry that anchors runs
   141	  records every ask; asks per run, per role, and per kind are read from
   142	  it. An ask that recurs across runs is a gap in a definition; the
   143	  answering role files the definition change, and the ask stops.
   144	- **Cancel** closes the run's work item with a reason and files the
   145	  resulting actions the outcomes demand.

   148	
   149	The compiler generates: the in-document flow diagram (typed inputs and
   150	outputs on every node; the result on the end node) and the skill —

   153	diagram, one section per step with the prompt verbatim). Conformance
   154	check: re-run the compiler and diff.
   155	
   156	## Commitment (Definition of Done)
   157	
   158	A process definition is done when it compiles — every `$ref` resolves,
   159	the diagram and renderings generate, `result` (if declared) names a data
   160	value — and every loop declares its exit. **Consequence on failure:** it
   161	cannot be dispatched, carried by a skill, or cited by a check.
   162	
   163	## Sources

   166	records with typed inputs/outputs); CNCF Serverless Workflow
   167	(data-condition transitions); CEL — Common Expression Language
   168	(mechanically translatable conditions); Essence-style state exits plus a
   169	round cap (the dual-exit rule).

   174	  byte-stable. *(Commitment)*

   177	- Every loop has labeled success and/or cap exits. *(§The steps section)*

===== discovery-conversation ===== 1 --- 2 type: process-definition 3 id: discovery-conversation-process 4 owner: product-authority 5 status: approved 6 approved: 2026-08-22 7 version: 8 8 created: 2026-08-22 9 updated: 2026-08-31 10 produces: [session-record, initiative] 11 condition-language: cel 12 hold-after: P7D 13 --- 14 15 # Process: Discovery conversation 16 17 **Purpose:** Conduct a bounded discovery dialogue in a declared form — 18 brainstorm (the first form), interview, or review of evidence: the 19 authority explores direction with the lead-pm as interlocutor, nothing 20 is operationalized before convergence, the session record anchors the 21 conversation, and a converged discovery leaves an initiative recorded 22 `proposed` — or `proposed` and then `cancelled` in the same document 23 when the request is declined, so the record of the decline survives. 24 25 **Guiding statement:** Engage the authority's statements as an 26 interlocutor; record and launch only after convergence. 27 28 **Outcomes:** 29 - O1. No work is launched and no definition is written before the 30 authority converges — witnessed by the `route` branches: the handoff 31 is reachable only from the authority's own classification. 32 - O2. The conversation closes onto a validated session record carrying 33 its produced and revised lists — witnessed by the `handoff` 34 sub-process, whose child validates the record before landing it. 35 - O3. Only the authority converges, closes, or cancels — witnessed by 36 the `route` branches. 37 - O4. An inactive conversation holds instead of dangling — witnessed by 38 `hold-after` and the run lifecycle. 39 - O5. A converged discovery returns an initiative recorded `proposed` 40 (or `proposed` then `cancelled` with the authority's reason when the 41 request is declined); a close without convergence lands the session 42 record and frames nothing — witnessed by `route-frame`, which 43 reaches `frame` only from the authority's converge classification. 44 45 **Roles:** product-authority (human-held role — explores, converges, and owns 46 the exclusive right to close or cancel). lead-pm — held by the same 47 person; its agent steps assist: `engage` prepares the reflection — 48 probes, names tensions, offers options with a recommendation, keeps the 49 draft record's quotes and state current — and the authority decides 50 what converges. The agent operationalizes nothing. 51 52 ## Flow (compiled) 53 54 Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not 55 edit by hand. 56 57 ```mermaid 58 flowchart TD 59 open["Open the work item — runtime

**Verdict: findings**

**Finding 1 — worst**
- File: `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/product-flow.md` (with `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md` frame step)
- Quote: `- label: "framed — an initiative stands proposed"` / `when: initiative != ""`
- Defect: A declined request is deliberately returned by discovery's `frame` step as a non-empty path recorded `proposed` then `cancelled` in the same document, so `route-discover`'s emptiness test sends a cancelled initiative through the entire initiative-check — attach steps writing into a cancelled document and the authority put to a bet decide whose record step's "planned" is not guarded to write only over `proposed` — before `route-bet`'s else finally ends the run, contradicting the branch label and O4's claim that a cancelled discovery ends with the records standing.

**Finding 2**
- File: `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md` (defeats the round-1 repair in product-flow.md)
- Quote: `initiative: {type: string, format: uri-reference}` (no `initial`)
- Defect: On the close-without-convergence and cancel paths the child ends without `frame` ever setting its result value `initiative`, and since the typedef says a sub-process step's "outputs receive the child's result", the parent's round-1 repair (`initiative: {... initial: ""}`) is overwritten by an undefined value — `route-discover`'s `initiative != ""` guard rests on an unstated convention; the coherent fix is `initial: ""` on the child's `initiative`.

**Finding 3**
- File: `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/product-flow.md`
- Quote: `the status feature_status of the feature just processed` (more-features prompt)
- Defect: On the checked→assign path `feature_status` was read at `read-feature` *before* the assignment sub-process, which can leave the feature `assigned` or `returned` (unowned scenarios / conflict), so the prompt presents a stale "checked" as the just-processed feature's status — the judgment survives only because the repository read happens to carry the true value, which the prompt does not say.

**Finding 4**
- File: `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/feature-authoring.md` (v4 draft step, against product-flow's returned loop)
- Quote: `add the feature's id to the initiative's Features section` / more-features: `a returned feature to author again`
- Defect: The re-author pass hands feature-authoring only `initiative` and `repository` — nothing identifies the returned feature — and `draft`'s prompt states only the new-feature form (unconditionally writing a feature and adding its id to §6), so authoring a returned feature again is undefined: the agent either duplicates the id in §6 or drafts a fresh feature instead of the repair the PO's "another" judgment intended.

**Finding 5 — minor**
- File: `/home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/product-flow.md`
- Quote: `produces: [initiative, feature, backlog-order]`
- Defect: Every product-flow run executes `discover`, whose child lands a session-record (`produces: [session-record, initiative]`), so under the typedef's definition of `produces` ("artifact types a run creates") the parent's list omits `session-record`.

**Everything else screened clean**, specifically:
- Part 1: frontmatter conforms; all six sub-process steps use the defined `run-by: {execution: sub-process, ...}` form; every routed status (`planned`, `checked`, `returned`) is one the named child's record/return steps write at that value; the else paths otherwise cover exactly `proposed`/`cancelled`, `returned`/`pending-definition` (prose note present); CEL well-formed; no dead branch rows; all four derived-check rows cite existing witnesses; the loop carries labeled success and failsafe (cap) exits; the only prompt (`more-features`) references only declared inputs.
- Compiler dry-run in the scratchpad: diagram and SKILL.md both regenerate byte-stable against the committed files (digest f43c7786468c); the skill's 15 steps, prompts, and branches match the definition exactly and declare themselves generated.
- Part 2: all four positional input lists match the children's parameter orders exactly (`initiative_criteria`/`feature_criteria`/`order_criteria` → `criteria_path`); the §6 write (feature-authoring v4 draft) and the initiative typedef v9's §6 writer clause cohere and support `more-features`; po-output-check's `active` write (only over `planned`) is idempotent across later passes; no other hand-off loses a needed value.
- Part 3: every approval the primer claims is true in the corpus (all six sub-processes, the initiative/feature/backlog-order/product-decision-record chains including fitness sets and guidelines, the four roles) once the batch's block approval lands product-flow; the disclosed post-cap/post-approval repairs (feature-authoring v4, initiative v9, discovery v8, initiative-check v4) all match their history entries and are covered by this screen; the primer's open list matches the corpus's actual draft files (experience records, interaction-conformance-check, reconcile-side `completed` amendment).
